And so union labor also, something that I believe is near and dear to my heart. And if we could focus on the middle class, if we can focus on workers when we talk about renewable energies and new economies, when we talk about American jobs plan or an infrastructure bill, if we're bringing American workers along and we have a by American provision, and we focus on the domestic steel and manufacturing. of what is going on in making sure that when we rebuild our roads, bridges, waterways, dams, water pipelines, infrastructure, our electricity grid that we bring workers along. If we do that, I believe that will chip away at the divide. So the PRO Act has a lot to do with giving unions the right to collectively bargain, to have fair elections, to put themselves in a position to regain ground that may have been taken away from unions' bargaining rights. over the last decade or so. You had mentioned Indiana and one of the first states to pass the right to work. So some might say, well, who might that impact? If you can go back in history, and I was there on the Indiana State Capitol stairs, there were over 15,000 men and women who showed up to protest the Right to Work Act, 15,000. The entire state capital was full of people on the outside and on the lawn and inside. And so we must remember that the middle class and working men and women and having the ability to have a fair wage is what's at stake. And so I'd be happy to have this discussion and dive into it, but that's a little bit of my perspective of where we come from.
